diagnosis:
The kubelet service on one worker node was stopped; the node itself (its container runtime and the containers already running) is still up. Without the kubelet the node posts no status: after about 40 s the node controller marks it NotReady, taints it node.kubernetes.io/unreachable, and marks its pods not ready, which removes them from their Services' endpoints, so the services running there fail. After the 300 s toleration the pods are evicted and recreated on the other worker; they stay Terminating on the dead node. Commands that go through the kubelet (kubectl logs/exec on that node's pods) fail with connection refused on port 10250. The fix is to start the kubelet on the node again (systemctl start kubelet on the machine), which needs access to the node itself.

Every product query waits behind the lock until the role's 3 s lock_timeout cancels it, so every product page fails. The job retries in a loop, so ending only its database session gets the lock taken again within seconds; deleting only the job leaves its session running (Postgres does not notice the vanished client while the statement runs), still holding the lock. Without the kubelet the node posts no status: after about 40 s the node controller marks it NotReady, taints it node.kubernetes.io/unreachable, and marks its pods not ready, which removes them from their Services' endpoints, so the services running there fail.
